findings.title: Deleting the cache doesn't refresh connectedCalendars, so the old "Last updated" timestamp stays on screen where onChanged isn't passed
findings.body: `deleteCacheMutation.onSuccess` only calls `onSuccess?.()`. Unlike `disconnectMutation` (lines 61-64), it never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. In CalendarListContainer, `onChanged` does that invalidation (apps/web/components/apps/CalendarListContainer.tsx:79-88). EventAdvancedTab renders `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` without `onChanged` (packages/features/eventtypes/components/tabs/advanced/EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372-375). On that page the cache section is still shown, because `hasCache` doesn't depend on `disableConnectionModification`. So after a successful delete the user gets the "Cache deleted successfully" toast, but the dropdown keeps showing the old "Last updated" timestamp and the delete action. Fix: add the same `onSettled` invalidation of `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` that the disconnect mutation already uses.

findings.title: Does `updateMany` with empty `data` actually bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`?
findings.body: The comment says this call updates `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` for every calendar under the credential, but it passes `data: {}`. As far as I know, Prisma's engine skips the write and doesn't set `@updatedAt` when the update arguments are empty, so this may do nothing. If the timestamp matters, set `updatedAt: new Date()` explicitly. Also, the newly selected `updatedAt`/`googleChannelId` fields (packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts:899-900) don't seem to be used by any UI in this PR. What does this write feed? If nothing reads it, it's an extra write on every webhook-driven cache fill and could be removed.

findings.title: Ownership failure throws a plain Error, which tRPC returns as a 500
findings.body: A credential that isn't found or isn't owned by the user is an expected client error. Throwing a plain `Error` makes tRPC report INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR and log it as a server fault. Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or FORBIDDEN) instead, as other viewer handlers do.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is always formatted with the en-US locale and the browser timezone
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)` ignores the user's locale (`useLocale` is already in scope) and their profile timezone. Non-US users see the date in US order (M/D/YY), which is easy to misread. Use the locale from `useLocale()` and the user's timezone.

findings.title: Script works only on macOS and only from one working directory
findings.body: `sed -i ''` is BSD sed syntax. GNU sed on Linux reads `''` as the script and fails, so `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` never gets updated. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved against the caller's working directory, not the script's location. Run from the repo root (`scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`), it creates or edits a `.env` one level above the repository. Resolve the path from `$(dirname "$0")` and use a portable in-place edit. Separately, `cleanup` always runs `exit 0`, so the failure branches (lines 49 and 58) report success to the caller.

contracts.action: User confirms "Delete cached data" in the credential dropdown
contracts.equivalent_path: disconnectMutation in the same component (lines 53-65): toast, onSuccess, then onSettled invalidates connectedCalendars and integrations
contracts.before_after: Disconnect invalidates connectedCalendars in onSettled. Delete-cache only calls the optional onSuccess prop, so the refresh depends on the caller passing onChanged.
contracts.visible_effect: Toast appears. In CalendarListContainer, onChanged invalidates connectedCalendars, so the timestamp disappears. In EventAdvancedTab no onChanged is passed, so the old timestamp and delete action stay on screen.
contracts.failure_mode: onError shows the error_deleting_cache toast. The dialog is already closed and nothing else changes. No silent loss.

contracts.action: deleteCache handler deletes all CalendarCache rows for a credential
contracts.before_after: Ownership is checked right before the delete (credential id + userId). The delete is scoped to that credentialId only. The cache is regenerated on the next fetch or webhook.
contracts.visible_effect: Rows are removed. The status reaches the UI only through the connectedCalendars refetch.
contracts.failure_mode: A missing or foreign credential throws a plain Error, which tRPC returns as a 500. A DB failure propagates to the client's onError toast.

contracts.action: connectedCalendars attaches cacheUpdatedAt from the CalendarCache groupBy
contracts.equivalent_path: Cache lookup via CalendarCacheRepository.getCachedAvailability, which uses userId for in-memory delegation credentials
contracts.before_after: The groupBy filters by credentialId only. In-memory delegation credentials have no DB credentialId, so they get no status and the cache item is hidden. This is consistent with deleteCache, which requires a DB credential.
contracts.visible_effect: Google calendar cards show a dropdown with the cache status when rows exist.
contracts.failure_mode: A groupBy failure fails the whole connectedCalendars query, so the calendar list fails to load.

contracts.action: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache bumps SelectedCalendar.updatedAt via updateMany with empty data
contracts.visible_effect: No UI in this PR reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt.
contracts.failure_mode: If it throws, fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache rejects after the cache is already written.
contracts.open_question: Does Prisma set @updatedAt when updateMany is called with data {}?

summary: The PR adds cache-status display and a "delete cached data" action for Google calendar credentials. Main defect: the delete mutation never invalidates connectedCalendars itself, so in the event-type Advanced tab (no onChanged passed) the old cache timestamp stays on screen after a successful delete. Smaller points: the SelectedCalendar.updatedAt bump with empty data may be a no-op; the handler returns a 500 on an ownership miss; the timestamp is hardcoded to en-US; and the dev script works only with macOS sed and from one working directory.
